what: A quick blind score by the author on the six questions of 2026-11-16-six-questions.json. Per question, 7 skill-only mechanisms the judge kept in both passes (grouping opus-1) and 7 plain-asking mechanisms were drawn at random (seed 20261116) and shuffled; 84 items in all.

how.shown: each mechanism as its representative idea, rewritten by an Opus sub-agent per question into a title of at most 20 characters and one or two sentences of at most 70, with method wording removed; the rewriter did not know the source
how.answer: one key per item: 1 had not thought of it and worth trying, 2 had thought of it and worth trying, 3 not worth trying, 4 unclear

reading: New and worth trying: 33 of 42 skill-only mechanisms and 31 of 42 plain-asking ones. No real difference.
Already thought of: 2 of 42 skill-only against 8 of 42 plain-asking. Not worth trying: 7 against 3. Neither difference is clear with 42 items a side (p 0.09 and 0.31).

On these questions most plain-asking ideas were also new to the author, unlike the CLI question where the author knew the field. The rate per mechanism is about equal; the skill reaches about three times as many mechanisms.
limits: the author is not an expert in most of these fields
the rewrite cut minor steps (pilots, checks) to fit 70 characters
rates are per sampled mechanism, not per run
